caption: System Architecture of the JAPZ Inventory Module
description: Figure 1 shows how Inventory Staff access the inventory interface. The Express API checks permissions and processes stock, recipe, report, and settings requests, while Sequelize stores and retrieves inventory records in MySQL.

caption: Core Inventory Classes and Relationships
description: Figure 2 shows the main classes used to receive and track supplies. A receipt contains delivery lines, each linked to an item and batch; movements record quantity changes. Supporting classes handle counts, waste reports, recipes, reservations, and settings.

name: Component Diagram
caption: Components of the Inventory Module
description: Figure 3 shows the software components that support inventory operations. Inventory screens use a shared data provider and HTTP client to access the API. The router works with access checks, inventory services, and database models to process requests.

name: Deployment Diagram
caption: Local Deployment of the Inventory Module
description: Figure 4 shows the configured local deployment of the inventory module. Staff use a browser to access the React application, which communicates with the Express API. The backend reads and saves inventory data in MySQL through Sequelize.

caption: Example Objects After Receiving Flour
description: Figure 5 presents an illustrative stock receipt for five kilograms of flour. The system converts the delivery to 5,000 grams and links the supplier, receipt, line, batch, and movement records. These sample values demonstrate the model and are not actual business records.

name: Package Diagram
caption: Packages of the Inventory Module
description: Figure 6 groups the inventory source into interface, client, route, service, and model packages. The dependencies show how inventory pages reach the backend and database. This organization separates screen behavior, business rules, and data storage.

name: Composite Structure Diagram
caption: Internal Collaboration Within the Inventory API
description: Figure 7 shows the collaborating parts inside the inventory API. Access checks pass authorized requests to route handlers, which call inventory services and models. The HTTP and SQL ports represent the module boundaries used for requests and persistence.

caption: Inventory Documentation Profile
description: Figure 8 defines inventory-specific stereotypes for UML documentation. InventoryRecord identifies stored records, StockService identifies service components, and StockOperation identifies stock actions. These labels are modeling conventions and are not an additional application feature.

name: Data Flow Diagram (DFD)
caption: Inventory Data Flow
description: Figure 9 shows how inventory information moves between staff, processes, and data stores. Supply maintenance saves item and supplier records, while stock operations update receipts, batches, and movements. The reporting process reads these records to display balances and stock history.

name: Use Case Diagram
caption: Inventory Staff Use Cases
description: Figure 10 shows the inventory goals available to Inventory Staff. Receiving includes delivery validation and unit conversion; count review and CSV export extend the related goals when their conditions apply. Admin handles required count approvals and movement reversals.

name: Activity Diagram

ops.s: Choose filters and read stock data

Save changes together
or queue count for review

caption: Main Activity Flow of the Inventory Module
description: Figure 11 presents the main Inventory Staff workflow after authentication. Staff can record stock operations or view balances, history, and reports. Stock changes are validated and saved together, while counts that require approval remain pending until Admin review.

name: Sequence Diagram

ops.s: Return the original receipt without duplicating stock
Rollback transaction and return an error

caption: Sequence of a Successful Stock Receipt
description: Figure 12 shows the order of messages during a new stock receipt. The interface submits the delivery and request ID, the backend validates and saves the stock changes, and the database commits the transaction. The saved receipt is returned so the interface can refresh the display.

name: State Machine Diagram
caption: Stock Count Status Changes
description: Figure 13 shows the implemented stock count states: pending, applied, rejected, and stale. A count applies immediately when review is unnecessary; otherwise, Admin reviews it. Approval changes the balance only when the stock version and reserved quantities remain valid.

name: Communication Diagram
caption: Object Communication During Receiving
description: Figure 14 shows the collaborating objects in a stock receipt. Numbered messages follow the request from Inventory Staff to the interface, router, service, and database. The service saves the receipt and stock changes, then returns the result to the interface.

name: Interaction Overview Diagram

ops.s:

caption: Overview of Inventory Receiving Interactions
description: Figure 15 combines activity decisions with the interactions used by the inventory module. Authentication precedes stock receiving, and a successful receipt is followed by a balance refresh. The receiving interaction is expanded in Figure 12; denied access ends the current attempt.

name: Timing Diagram

ops.s: Times model the order of work; they are not measured performance targets.

caption: Timing of the Stock Receiving Process
description: Figure 16 models when each participant is active during a stock receipt: submission, authorization, validation, persistence, and display. The stepped timelines show how the interface, backend, and database coordinate. The four-second timeline is illustrative and does not represent measured response times.

name: Requirement Diagram (SysML)

ops.s:
Inventory Management
Support accurate, controlled stock operations.

Approved Inventory / Admin
may change inventory.

Commit related records together;
repeat requests do not duplicate stock.

Exclude expired / held batches
and protect reserved stock.

Reject stale counts and apply
the configured approval policy.

Store quantity changes,
actor, and reason.

caption: Requirements of the Inventory Module
description: Figure 17 derives the inventory module’s supporting requirements from its overall purpose. The requirements cover access control, reliable receiving, safe availability, controlled counts, and traceable history. Satisfy links identify the implementation elements responsible for these rules.
